environment.description: Application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB, connecting to PostgreSQL 15 on RDS via RDS Proxy. The database connection uses IAM authentication with a dedicated PostgreSQL role 'app_ro_svc' that was provisioned with a restricted grant set. The role was created with: CREATE ROLE app_ro_svc LOGIN; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_ro_svc; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO app_ro_svc; The role has no membership in any other role and pg_hba.conf enforces method=md5 for this user from the RDS Proxy CIDR only. Additionally, the RDS instance has a custom parameter group with 'log_statement=all' and the RDS Proxy connection pool is pinned to this single role regardless of application-level connection string changes. Note: the ALB does NOT have any WAF rules attached — traffic filtering is not the mitigation strategy here.

config.database: PostgreSQL 15 on RDS, custom parameter group (log_statement=all)
config.db_grants: GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_ro_svc; no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE
config.connection: RDS Proxy with IAM auth, pinned to app_ro_svc role
config.pg_hba: host all app_ro_svc 10.0.64.0/20 md5 (RDS Proxy subnet only)
config.network: ECS Fargate -> RDS Proxy -> RDS, no direct DB access
config.auth: X-User-Role header trusted from client (same vulnerability exists)
